newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures slump as longs liquidate in US.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures slump as longs liquidate in US.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil futures tumbled shortly after the NYMEX opened as news Iraq had completed its aid hand-out plan under the U.N. food-for-oil deal encouraged a burst of long liquidation, brokers said.
August Brent was trading down 57 cents at a session low of $18.35 a barrel at 1459 GMT, while July gas oil was $3.00 a tonne down at $164.50.
"The selling started in New York with the locals getting rid of their longs built up yesterday," said one broker.
"Iraq sales are getting closer, but stops were triggered at support levels which has made it look worse than it really is."

Iraq's United Nations coordinator said on Thursday that Baghdad and the U.N. have completed aid distribution plans to cover the next six months of oil exports and would send them to the U.N. for approval soon.
Finalisation of the plan is the next step towards the long-delayed resumption of oil sales.
Dealers said that profit-taking ahead of the Fourth of July holiday weekend in the United States was expected after four straight days of gains on the oil market.
"There's a long weekend coming up and I think this is seen as a good reason to take profits," a broker said.
"There was some good upwards momentum yesterday but people don't want to risk being long over the weekend."
